### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A01 appeared in about 46 in 100 traces (roughly 0.9 occurrences per trace); in the later window, A01 is not observed at all. [OCC001, POS001]
- In the later window, A13 — absent from the earlier window — appears in about 53 in 100 traces (about 1.1 occurrences per trace) at a mean relative position of about 0.68 of the trace, the same position A01 previously occupied (about 0.68). [OCC001, OCC010, POS001, POS012]
- A10's outgoing transitions changed completely: earlier they all led to A01, in the later window they all lead to A13, and A13 leads exclusively to A03 — the edge A01 previously had (all of A01's transitions went to A03). [DIR001, DIR010, DIR011]
- A13 now co-occurs with the partners A01 used to have: together with A02, A03, A09, A10 and A11 in about 53 in 100 traces (A01 previously co-occurred with each in about 46 in 100), and partially with A04–A08 and A12; every earlier A01 relation is gone. [REL009, REL012, REL022, REL032, REL070, REL073, REL075]
- The affected segment also runs more often: A10 rises from about 46 to 53 in 100 traces and from about 0.9 to 1.1 occurrences per trace, with more repetition (recurrence about 0.21 to 0.31). [OCC008, OCC010, REL068]
- A03 occurs slightly more often per trace (about 1.9 to 2.1) and repeats more (recurrence about 0.46 to 0.53); its outgoing transitions shift a little from A11 (about 52% to 48% of them) toward A10 (about 48% to 53%). [OCC002, DIR003]
- Smaller shifts: participation dips slightly for A04 (about 48 to 46 in 100 traces), A07 (about 29 to 26) and A12 (about 24 to 21); A04, A05, A06 and A12 show small moves toward earlier trace positions; and around A03 fixed orders became slightly more mixed (e.g., A02 before A03 in 54% vs 47% of traces, interleaved/repeated 46% vs 53%, similarly for A03 with A09 and A11). [OCC003, OCC006, OCC009, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS011, REL013, REL028, REL030]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A01 was replaced by A13 at the same point of the process: the earlier segment A10 → A01 → A03, present in about 46 in 100 traces, appears in the later window as A10 → A13 → A03 in about 53 in 100 traces. The replacement is shown directly by A10's outgoing transitions switching entirely from A01 to A13 and by A13's exclusive edge to A03, and it is consistent across occurrence (A01 at zero, A13 new), position (A13 takes over A01's mean relative position of about 0.68) and relations (A13 inherits A01's co-occurrence partners) — these indicator families describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. The key items all reach the maximum empirical strength (about 0.995, exceeding all 200 random re-splits), and an activity present in 92 of 200 traces falling to zero observations is not what sampling variability produces. Limitations: zero participation strictly establishes only that A01 was not observed in the later window, and the evidence cannot distinguish a genuine substitution from A01 simply being relabelled as A13, nor exclude that A01 persists at a rate too low to be sampled. [OCC001, OCC010, DIR001, DIR010, DIR011, POS001, POS012, REL012, REL073]

Other differences: A03 occurs and repeats somewhat more often, with fixed orderings around it becoming slightly more mixed (A02/A03, A03/A09, A03/A11, each shifting about 7 in 100 traces from fixed order toward interleaved/repeated); A04, A07 and A12 participate slightly less often, and A04, A05, A06 and A12 show small shifts toward earlier trace positions. These are modest changes alongside the main difference. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC006, OCC009, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS011, REL013, REL028, REL030]
